question.prompt:
The table below gives the percent of students in each grade at Annville and Cleona elementary schools:

\[\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline & K & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6\\ \hline \text{Annville} & 16\% & 15\% & 15\% & 14\% & 13\% & 16\% & 11\%\\ \hline \text{Cleona} & 12\% & 15\% & 14\% & 13\% & 15\% & 14\% & 17\%\\ \hline\end{array}\]

Annville has \(100\) students and Cleona has \(200\) students. In the two schools combined, what percent of the students are in grade \(6?\)

solutions.explanation:
The schools have different numbers of students, so first convert each school's percentage into a number of sixth graders. Annville has \(11\%\cdot100=11\) sixth graders, and Cleona has \(17\%\cdot200=34\).

Together, the schools have \(11+34=45\) sixth graders and \(100+200=300\) students. Thus the percentage in grade \(6\) is
\[
\frac{45}{300}\cdot100\%=15\%.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{15\%}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Find the student counts first
